items.readable_text:
Content:
Whenever two right triangles are similar, their trigonometric ratios are equal for corresponding angles. This provides a convenient tool for solving problems involving lengths and angles in similar right triangles.

Content:
To demonstrate, consider the two triangles shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5fde56e05b874f9d63d3543ee489ce5b]

Content:
Suppose we wish to compute the following trigonometric ratio:

Content:
[MATH: \tan D]

Content:
At first glance, it may seem that we don't have enough information to find [MATH: \tan D] since both the opposite side, [MATH: EF,] and the adjacent side, [MATH: DF,] are unknown.

Content:
However, we can compute [MATH: \tan D] by showing that the two triangles are similar and then finding the tangent of the angle corresponding to [MATH: D.]

Content:
Notice we have two congruent angles:

Content:
[MATH: \angle B\cong \angle F, \qquad \angle C \cong \angle E]

Content:
Therefore, the two triangles are similar by the AA (Angle-Angle) criterion:

Content:
[MATH: \triangle ABC \sim \triangle DFE]

Content:
Consequently,

Content:
[MATH: \angle A\cong\angle D.]

Content:
Notice that we have enough information to find [MATH: \tan A{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \tan A = (BC)/(AB) = (4)/(3)]

Content:
Therefore, since [MATH: A] and [MATH: D] have equal measure, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: \tan D = \dfrac43.]

items.title: Evaluating a Trigonometric Ratio Given Two Similar Right Triangles

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the value of [MATH: \sec{F}.]
EXPLANATION

In the right triangles [MATH: \triangle ABC] and [MATH: \triangle DEF,] we have two pairs of congruent angles:

  • [MATH: \angle B \cong \angle E,] since they are both right angles, and

  • [MATH: \angle A\cong \angle D.]

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF] by AA, and consequently, [MATH: \angle F\cong\angle C.]

So we have

[MATH: \cos{F} = \cos{C} = \dfrac{BC}{AC} = \dfrac{6}{10}=\dfrac{3}{5},]

and finally, [MATH: \sec{F} = \dfrac{1}{\cos{F}} = \dfrac{5}{3}.]

sections.normalized_html: Calculate the value of [MATH: \tan{\angle CBD}.]
EXPLANATION

In the triangles [MATH: \triangle BDC] and [MATH: \triangle ABC,] there are two pairs of congruent angles:

  • [MATH: \angle BDC \cong \angle ABC] since they are both right angles, and

  • [MATH: \angle C] is common to both triangles.

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle BDC \sim \triangle ABC] by AA, and consequently, [MATH: \angle CBD \cong \angle A.]

So, we have

[MATH: \tan (∠CBD)|= \tan A = (BC)/(AB) = (3)/(4).]

items.title: Finding a Trigonometric Ratio Using the Pythagorean Theorem

key_prerequisites.name: Calculating Trigonometric Ratios Using the Pythagorean Theorem

sections.normalized_html: Find the value of [MATH: \cos C.]
EXPLANATION

In the triangles [MATH: \triangle ADB] and [MATH: \triangle ABC,] there are two pairs of congruent angles:

  • [MATH: \angle ABC \cong \angle BDA] since they are both right angles, and

  • [MATH: \angle A] is common to both triangles.

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ADB \sim \triangle ABC] by AA. As a result, we have [MATH: \angle C\cong\angle ABD,] and consequently

[MATH: \cos C= \cos (\angle ABD) =\dfrac{BD}{AB}=\dfrac{5}{AB}.]

The value of [MATH: AB] is not given, but we can calculate it using the Pythagorean theorem on [MATH: \triangle ADB] as follows:

[MATH: AB|= sqrt(AD^{2} + BD^{2}); = sqrt((sqrt(11))^{2} + 5^{2}); = sqrt(11 + 25); = sqrt(36); = 6]

Finally, we get

[MATH: \cos C=\dfrac{5}{AB}=\dfrac{5}{6}.]

Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
Whenever two right triangles are similar, their trigonometric ratios are equal for corresponding angles. This provides a convenient tool for solving problems involving lengths and angles in similar right triangles.

Content:
To demonstrate, consider the two triangles shown below.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5fde56e05b874f9d63d3543ee489ce5b]

Content:
Suppose we wish to compute the following trigonometric ratio:

Content:
[MATH: \tan D]

Content:
At first glance, it may seem that we don't have enough information to find [MATH: \tan D] since both the opposite side, [MATH: EF,] and the adjacent side, [MATH: DF,] are unknown.

Content:
However, we can compute [MATH: \tan D] by showing that the two triangles are similar and then finding the tangent of the angle corresponding to [MATH: D.]

Content:
Notice we have two congruent angles:

Content:
[MATH: \angle B\cong \angle F, \qquad \angle C \cong \angle E]

Content:
Therefore, the two triangles are similar by the AA (Angle-Angle) criterion:

Content:
[MATH: \triangle ABC \sim \triangle DFE]

Content:
Consequently,

Content:
[MATH: \angle A\cong\angle D.]

Content:
Notice that we have enough information to find [MATH: \tan A{:}]

Content:
[MATH: \tan A = (BC)/(AB) = (4)/(3)]

Content:
Therefore, since [MATH: A] and [MATH: D] have equal measure, we conclude that

Content:
[MATH: \tan D = \dfrac43.]

Therefore, [MATH: \triangle ABC \sim \triangle DEF] by AA, and consequently, [MATH: \angle F\cong\angle C.]
